output.reason: A 68-year-old man with two weeks of worsening bilateral ankle swelling and new orthopnea for two nights is a plausible acute decompensated heart failure presentation requiring immediate emergency assessment with oxygen saturation, imaging and bloodwork that messaging cannot provide.
output.patientMessage: Go to the emergency department now. Worsening swelling in both ankles plus needing to sit up to breathe at night can mean fluid backing up from a heart or related problem, which needs same-hour tests and treatment. Have someone drive you rather than driving yourself. If you develop severe breathlessness at rest, chest pain, or fainting on the way, call 911 immediately.
differential: Acute decompensated heart failure with pulmonary congestion
Other volume-overload cause (kidney or liver disease)

redFlags.concern: Breathlessness at rest or on exertion during the day
